Order:

The case of the petitioner, as per the writ affidavit, is that he belongs to a displaced family affected by the Priyadarshini Jurala Project (PJP), having lost Ac. 0-05 guntas of ancestral agricultural land in Sy. No. 1200/2 and a dwelling house bearing No. 1-113, PJP No. 312, both of which were submerged due to the backwaters of the project.

The Government awarded compensation vide Award No. 3/1996 dated 03.01.1996 for the land and Award No. 42/2005 dated 25.05.2005 for the house, with partial disbursal of compensation (Rs. 13,634/- for the house and Rs. 4,783/- as first installment for land), promising Government employment under G.O.Ms.No.98, dated 15.04.1986,
which stipulates that one dependent of a displaced family--if there is no other earning member--shall be eligible for appointment to posts up to the level of Junior Assistant/Typist in Major & Medium Irrigation and Power Projects, subject to application within one year of actual displacement.

The petitioner, educated up to 7thclass and belonging to a poor family with agricultural background, submitted his employment application on 18.10.1996, within one year of the land Award, and another on 20.06.1997 at the request of the office of the 3rdrespondent- Superintending Engineer, PJP Circle No.1, Gadwal, and his name was listed at Sl. No. 80 of a 101-member roster of displaced persons.

However, by memo dated 18.10.1997, the District Collector's office informed him that his application was forwarded to respondent No.3 but wp_4684_2018 NBK, J was "not traceable," and instead attached another application dated 18.10.1997, which the petitioner disputes.

Petitioner alleges that vested interests in the offices of respondent Nos.2 and 3 deliberately misplaced his 1996 application and substituted it with the 1997 version to wrongly disqualify him on the ground that it was filed beyond the stipulated one- year period.

It is stated that in the minutes of the selection committee meeting dated 10.01.2008,
culminating in proceedings dated 10.04.2008, his name was deleted from the roster, yet others similarly situated, including respondent No.5 (Sl. No. 83), whose name also appeared in the deletion list, were appointed.
It is stated that his candidature was not considered under G.O.Ms.No.98.

He filed RTI applications on 20.10.2017 but evasive response was given citing non- availability of 1996 records, while records from 1997 were conveniently available, thereby petitioner's claim is being intentionally suppressed by officials.

Aggrieved by denial of employment despite fulfilling eligibility Maqbul , Maqabul Pasha vs The Government Of Telengana, on 28 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190878633/
1 under G.O.Ms.No.98, submission of timely application, and continuous follow-ups including numerous representations and filing of OA No. 8331/2011 before the A.P. Administrative Tribunal,
the petitioner now challenges the impugned proceedings dated 10.04.2008 and letter dated 09.11.2017 issued by respondent No.3 as arbitrary and illegal, and seeks a direction to consider his application dated 18.10.1996 for employment in terms of G.O.Ms.No.98 dated 15.04.1986.

Heard Mr. K. Durga Prasad, learned counsel for the petitioner; Ms. B. Annapurna, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Services-I;
wp_4684_2018 NBK, J and Mr. N. Ramesh, learned counsel for respondent No.5.
Perused the record.
3. A counter affidavit is filed by respondent No. 3 on behalf of respondents 1, 2, and 4, denying the petitioner's claims as untenable and misconceived.

The respondents rely on G.O. Ms. No. 98, dated 15.04.1986, which mandates that applications for employment by displaced persons must be submitted within one year of displacement, as per para 4(iii), and that only those losing cultivable land or having less than one acre are eligible, as per Memo No. 188/LAR-2/89-6, dated 19.04.1990.

The petitioner's land in Sy. No. 1200/2 (0.05 guntas) was acquired under Award No.3/1996, dated 03.01.1996, with compensation of Rs. 4,783/-, but his application dated 18.10.1997 was filed beyond the one-year limit, leading to rejection vide orders dated 10.04.2008,08.07.2010, and 28.03.2011.

The petitioner's subsequent claim regarding house acquisition (Award No. 42/2005, dated 25.05.2005) was also rejected as time-barred, and the AP Administrative Tribunal dismissed his challenge in OA No. 8331 of 2011 on 23.09.2014, upholding the rejection.

The District Selection Committee, constituted under G.O. Ms. No. 266, dated 19.09.1994, and modified by G.O. Ms. No.
135, dated 17.11.2009, reviewed applications, including the petitioner's and found him ineligible due to delayed submission and lack of ownership proof for the acquired house (Award No. 4/2012, dated 21.03.2012).

The respondents assert that the petitioner's name was rightly excluded from the 101-member list (Sl. No. 79) as his application violated the G.O.'s timeline, while eligible candidates like respondent No. 5 were duly appointed.

It is stated that WP No.4925 of wp_4684_2018 NBK, J 2012 involving similar delayed claims was dismissed, and therefore the present writ petition is also liable for dismissal as devoid of merit.
4.

An additional counter affidavit is filed by respondent No. 3 on behalf of respondents 1 and 2,
supplementing the earlier counter affidavit.

The respondents cite G.O. Ms. No. 38, dated 01.10.2021,
modifying the District Selection Committee composition per G.O. Ms. No. 45, dated 28.12.2020, and reiterate that the petitioner's claim under G.O. Ms. No.98, dated 15.04.1986, is inadmissible.

The petitioner's land in Sy. No.1200/2 (0.05 guntas) was acquired under Award No. 3/1996, dated 03.01.1996, with compensation of Rs. 4,783/-, but his application dated 18.10.1997 was filed beyond the one-year limit under para 4(iii) of the G.O.

Further, the petitioner, being the grandson of Smt.
Masum Bee (a pattadar), is ineligible per para 4(ii) of the G.O., as grandsons are not recognized as dependents, a position upheld in WA No. 1387 of 2011, dated 02.02.2012.

The respondents highlight that the petitioner's house (No. 2-87/3 and No. 279) was acquired under Award No. 4/2012, dated 21.03.2012, per G.O. Rt. No. 1050, dated 12.12.2007, but he lacks ownership proof, and Uppair village's designation as an "Affected Zone" under G.O. Ms. No. 68, dated 08.04.2005 (per WP No.

The respondents assert that the petitioner's delayed representation made on 27.11.2012 is invalid, and therefore the writ petition is liable to be dismissed.

A counter affidavit is filed by respondent No. 5opposing the writ petition and asserting that the petitioner's claims are untenable.

The respondent relies on G.O. Ms. No. 98, dated 15.04.1986,
which mandates that employment under the displaced persons quota is restricted to dependents (son, daughter, or spouse) of those whose land was acquired, provided applications are submitted within one year of displacement, as per para 4(iii); the petitioner failed to comply with this timeline,
rendering his claim invalid.

The respondent further cites G.O. Ms. No. 266, dated 19.09.1994, and G.O. Ms. No. 135, dated 17.11.2009, which outline the District Selection Committee's composition,
and Memo dated 07.10.1987, and Memo dated 19.04.1990, which specify eligibility criteria,
including compensation limits and land loss requirements.

The respondent clarifies that his own appointment as Junior Assistant vide Proceedings dated 09.08.2012 and subsequent promotion to Senior Assistant vide Proceedings dated 02.03.2016 were lawful, as his family's land was acquired under Award No. 3/96, dated 12.01.1996, and his application adhered to the G.O.'s stipulations.

He refutes the petitioner's allegation that his inclusion at Sl. No. 83 in the displaced persons list was improper, emphasizing that the petitioner's delayed application and ineligibility as a grandson justified the rejection.
6. A reply affidavit is filed by the petitionerrefuting the respondents' claims and reiterating his entitlement to employment under G.O. Ms. No. 98, dated 15.04.1986.

The petitioner asserts that he submitted his employment application on 18.10.1996, within the one-year deadline under para 4(iii)
of the G.O., but the respondents falsely allege it was filed on 18.10.1997, manipulating records (as evidenced by RTI wp_4684_2018 NBK, J responses denying access to the 1996 inward register while producing a disputed 1997 application).

It is stated that the respondents have irregularly appointed respondent No. 5 (Manneappa), whose name was initially rejected (Sl. No. 83 in the rejection list) for late submission, but later reinstated based on a fabricated acknowledgment slip dated 22.10.1996, while denying the petitioner (Sl. No. 79) the same concession.

7. Learned counsel for the petitionerwould essentially contend that the petitioner is entitled to employment under G.O. Ms. No. 98, dated 15.04.1986, as his land (Sy. No. 1200/2, measuring 0.05 guntas) and house (No. 1-113/PJP No. 312) were duly acquired under Award No. 3/1996 and Award No. 42/2005, with compensation paid accordingly, thereby qualifying him as a displaced family member eligible for the displaced persons quota.

It is contended that his application for employment was filed on 18.10.1996, well within the prescribed one- year period mandated by para 4(iii) of the G.O., and disputes the respondents' claim of a 1997 filing date, pointing to irregularities and manipulation in the records, as evidenced by contradictory RTI responses and the denial of access to the 1996 inward register.

It is contended that the respondents acted arbitrarily and Maqbul , Maqabul Pasha vs The Government Of Telengana, on 28 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190878633/
3 discriminately by initially rejecting the petitioner's application on the ground of delay while later accepting respondent No.5's claim despite similar or greater delay, relying on a fabricated acknowledgment slip.

sentences.text: 8. Learned counsel for the respondent No.3essentially contends that the petitioner's claims are wholly untenable and barred by law, as he failed to comply with the mandatory conditions prescribed under wp_4684_2018 NBK, J G.O.Ms. No. 98, dated 15.04.1986, which requires that applications for employment by displaced persons be submitted within one year of displacement, a condition the petitioner violated by filing his application on 18.10.1997, well beyond the stipulated period, rendering it time- barred.

Further, the petitioner's land in Sy. No. 1200/2 (0.05 guntas) was acquired under Award No. 3/1996 with compensation duly paid, yet he did not qualify as a dependent under the G.O., since being the grandson of the pattadar (Smt. Masum Bee), he is ineligible as per para 4(ii), a position upheld by this Court in WA No. 1387 of 2011.

The petitioner's claim based on house acquisition under Award No. 42/2005 also fails, as he lacks ownership proof,
and the affected area designation under G.O. Ms. No. 68, dated 08.04.2005, restricts benefits to financial compensation alone, excluding employment benefits.

The District Selection Committee,
constituted and reconstituted under relevant G.Os., consistently found the petitioner ineligible.

9. Learned counsel for the respondent No.5essentially contends that the petitioner's claims are baseless and contrary to the clear provisions of G.O. Ms. No. 98, dated 15.04.1986, which restricts employment under the displaced persons quota exclusively to dependents--son, daughter, or spouse--who submit applications within one year of displacement, a requirement the petitioner failed to meet, rendering his claim invalid.

Further, the respondent No.5's appointment as Junior Assistant and subsequent promotion were fully in accordance with the rules, as his family's land was acquired under Award No. 3/96 with proper compensation, and his application complied with the prescribed timelines and eligibility criteria under G.O. Ms. Nos. 266 and 135, as wp_4684_2018 NBK, J well as relevant memos.

The petitioner's contention that respondent No. 5's inclusion at Sl.
No. 83 was improper is unfounded, particularly given the petitioner's delayed application and ineligibility as a grandson, as highlighted in the additional counter affidavit; thus, the respondent urges the dismissal of the writ petition as devoid of merit.

10. Having considered the respective contentions and perused the record, it may be noted that the petitionerclaims entitlement to employment under the displaced persons quota as per G.O. Ms. No.
98, dated 15.04.1986, asserting that his land in Sy. No. 1200/2 (0.05 guntas) and house (No.
1-113/PJP No. 312) were acquired under Award No. 3/1996, dated 03.01.1996, and Award No.
42/2005, dated 25.05.2005, with compensation duly paid, and that his application for employment was submitted within the one-year time as prescribed under para 4(iii) of the G.O. Ms. Nos. 266 and 135, however, his claim has been rejected on the ground of delay and also for the reason of petitioner being grandson of the displaced person.

11. At this juncture, it is relevant to note that the Hon'ble Division Bench of this Court in W.A.No.1387 of 2011 has observed as follows:

sentences.text: The Government while considering representation of the displaced persons evolved the scheme of providing employment to the displaced person, his dependants namely son, daughter or spouse alone and accordingly issued GO Ms. No. 98 dated 15.4.1986.

Clauses 4(i) and (ii) of the said G.O. are relevant for the purpose of adjudication of the controversy involved, which read as under:
wp_4684_2018 NBK, J 4.
After careful examination and consideration, the following orders are issued in supersession of orders in GO Ms. No.676 Irrigation & Power Department dated 17.11.1978.

(i) Not more than 50% of the vacancies of the categories equivalent to Junior Assistants/Typists and the cadres below arising in major and medium irrigation and power projects shall be filled up by the displaced families/or their dependants of a respective projects duly following the reservation for various categories viz., SC, ST,
BC, Ex-Servicemen, Physically Handicapped and Meritorious Sportsmen, etc.
(ii) The candidates eligible for appointment under this scheme shall be the displaced persons or his/her son, daughter or spouse, there being no other earning member in the family 9.

Clause (i) above provides for filling up 50% of the vacancies in the categories equivalent to Junior Assistants/Typists and the cadres below arising in major and medium irrigation and power projects, to be filled by the displaced persons or their dependants in the respective projects duly following the reservation for various categories like Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Backward Classes,
Ex-Servicemen, Physically Handicapped and Meritorious Sportsmen, etc.

Clause (ii)
above speaks of eligibility criteria prescribed for the appointment under the scheme,
to be a displaced person, his/her son, daughter or spouse and there being no earning member in the family.
Clause 4(i) deals with the percentage of vacancies to be filled by the displaced persons or dependants after following the rule of reservation.

Therefore, we are of the opinion that clause 4(i) relates to filling up of 50% vacancies by the displaced families or their dependants while wp_4684_2018 NBK, J clause 4(ii) relates to the eligibility criteria for such appointments by the displaced persons or his/her son/daughter or spouse alone, if there being no other earning member in the family.
The grandson cannot be called as a dependant of the grandfather/land loser whose land was acquired.

The dependant of a land loser is only his/her spouse,
son and daughter, if they continue to be non-earning member of the family.

If the grandsons are also considered as eligible for appointment then there will not be an end to draw a line, as the great grandsons may also seek employment under the reserved 50% vacancies for the displaced families in the respective projects.
Therefore, we are of the opinion that the respondent is not entitled to be considered for the appointment under GO Ms. No. 98 dated 15.04.2006.

sentences.text: It may be noted that the petitioner made a claim in the year 2012, and further the petitioner is the grandson of the land oustee/displaced person, and therefore he is not eligible to claim employment under G.O.No.98 under displaced person or his spouse/son/daughter category.

Even assuming the application is submitted within the prescribed timeline, the application could not have been entertained primarily for the reason that he is does not fit into that definition under G.O.No.98 for claiming employment.
Furthermore, even the displaced/entitled dependent of the displaced person is required to submit his application within the prescribed timeline of one year.

The initial inclusion of the petitioner in the list of displaced persons, in whatever serial number it may be, is not material and cannot be a ground to canvass his case, forit is for the authorities to subsequently examine the application and process it in accordance with law, and therefore mere inclusion in the wp_4684_2018 NBK, J initial stages of the application does not per se make the petitioner entitled to employment.

Further, it is to be noted that the aspect of granting compensation for the land acquired and receiving the same by the beneficiary, and the aspect of making claim for employment in the capacity of displaced person are two different things.

It is common knowledge that, in certain cases, legal heirs may receive compensation in the absence of original owner; however, conversely,
the mere act of receiving the compensation/becoming a beneficiary of the Award does not automaticallymake the recipient a displaced person for the purpose of employment under G.O.No.98.

Further, not all the displaced persons can claim employment, and there are certain criteria enumerated under the G.O. No.98 which need to be fulfilled by the displaced person to qualify for consideration for employment.
Further, there is another rider that the claims for employment would be considered only if there is no earning member in the displaced persons family.

In the instant case, the petitioner cannot be categorized a displaced person or a dependent of displaced person as defined under the G.O.No.98 for the purpose of employment, as he is neither the dependent spouse nor the dependent son/daughter of the displaced person for the purposes of employment; and therefore, rejecting his application for employment under displaced persons category cannot be said to be arbitrary or illegal.

In that view of the matter, and also the criteria enumerated in G.O.No.98, and also the law laid down by the Hon'ble Division Bench in W.A.No.1387 of 2011, this Court does not see any illegality in the impugned proceedings rejecting the claim of the petitioner for employment.
Accordingly, the writ petition is dismissed.
No costs.

Miscellaneous petitions, if any pending,
shall stand closed.
